newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's president continues search for new PM.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's president continues search for new PM.

text.p: Slovenian President Milan Kucan on Tuesday continued talks to determine who should lead the next government, his spokeswoman Spela Furlan said.
"Today he will meet the president of parliament Janez Podobnik, while he will hold another round of talks with parliamentary parties next Monday," Furlan told Reuters.

The president met the governor of the Bank of Slovenia France Arhar and the Constitutional Court president Anton Jerovsek on Monday in a bid to end the political impasse that followed the November 10 general elections.

Although Kucan earlier held two rounds of talks with parliamentary parties, support in parliament was divided between current Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats and Marjan Podobnik, head of the conservative People's Party.

The Liberal Democrats are the strongest single party with 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats, while the People's Party is the biggest of the three rightist parties that have formed the "Spring" alliance. Together they hold 45 seats, just one short of an absolute majority.
Last week Kucan, who has to name a candidate by January 3, said he would do so before the end of the year. Sources close to the president expect him to take a decision on December 30 or 31.
